question.problem: Make $c$ the subject of the equation $-6a=9b-2c.$
question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $c,$ so we will treat the other variables $a$ and $b$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $c.$

First, we add $2c$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6a & =9b-2c \\ -6a+2c & =9b-2c+2c \\ -6a+2c & =9b\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $6a$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6a+2c & =9b \\ -6a+2c+6a & =9b+6a \\ 2c & =9b+6a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2c & =9b+6a \\ \frac{2c}{2} & =\frac{9b+6a}{2} \\ c & =\frac{9b+6a}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
